items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: He said, well, Stilman is away again, he's out of town, we'll have to wait for him to get back.

ctx.x: I borrowed--what the hell was it--two thousand dollars, three thousand dollars--with the understanding that they were going to pay me a salary of five hundred a week, starting immediately and that after two months, I think it was, I would accept half salary until the debt was paid back. So we shook hands on the agreement, the end of the first week everybody gets their checks except me. I said, 'where's my check, Boyd?' 'Oh, Stirling is out of town, he'll be back next week, we'll give you double

next week, but hey look, you got five hundred dollars knocked off your debt already." I said "that's not the point, it's not our agreement; our agreement was for full salary for two months and then half salary until it's paid off." "Well, he'll be back and we'll get it straightened out." I said I want a guarantee that I'm going to get the right money next week. You've got it. Next week comes, no check again. I said where's my money, how am I going to live? Ain't this great, you paid back a thousand already. I…
So the following week, no check-- (tape went blank for a few seconds)--"I have one thing to say to you and that is goodbye." That was it.
